record.textual_conclusion:
Abstract: ...The transfer learning approach consistently performed well on the ArSL dataset and outperformed other CNN models. ResNet and InceptionResNet obtained a comparably high performance of 98%. By combining the concepts of transformer-based architecture and pretraining, ViT and Swin leveraged the strengths of both architectures and reduced the number of parameters required for training, making them more efficient and stable than other models and existing studies for ArSL classification.

Conclusion: ... Experimental results revealed that the transfer learning approach, using both pretrained models and vision transformers, achieved a higher accuracy compared to traditional CNN-based deep learning models. Although the pretrained models performed better in terms of accuracy, the vision transformers exhibited more consistent learning. The findings suggest that using recently designed pretrained models such as BiT and InceptionResNet, as well as vision transformers like ViT and Swin, can enhance accuracy, parameter efficiency, feature reuse, scalability, and overall performance in ArSL classification tasks.

status.numerical_agreement_basis: Assess the 28 first/final accuracy targets of the 14 models other than VGG16 and VGG19 using ordinary top-1 accuracy under documented reconstruction assumptions. All differ from the published fractions by more than 0.00005, the half-unit rounding interval for four decimal places. This is a descriptive comparison at printed precision, not a statistical significance test. The four VGG accuracy targets are excluded by reviewer decision (classifier-head-review gate); the remaining 96 metric targets are not assessed because their definitions are unresolved.

gates.reason: Code review found that the classifier heads differ from the paper's stated architecture, and VGG16/VGG19 collapsed to a single predicted class with chance-level training loss from epoch one.
evidence: Paper methodology: fine-tuning 'using an added dense layer and one classification layer'; Table 4 CNN-3 head.
scripts/models.py: transfer heads end in Dense(32, softmax) on pooled features; CNN-3 adds Dense(128).
full-vgg16 and full-vgg19: identical probabilities for all 5404 validation images at epochs 1 and 10; final training loss 3.4601 (ln 32 = 3.4657).

The attribution has not been tested with a corrected run.

deviations.description: All reconstruction choices in README.md approved on 2026-11-04; original targets remain not produced because approval does not recover the original protocol.

Cross-process resume verification compares all checkpoint tensors exactly and records inference differences with a 0.001 absolute guard. TensorFlow float32/TF32 kernels may differ across GPU processes; training and model parameters are unchanged. Hypothesis is being tested. Follow-up resume-check-xception-state verified 555 tensors bit-for-bit, zero prediction difference on that process, and successful next optimizer step.
Add opencv-python-headless==4.8.1.78 to satisfy a demonstrated undeclared vit-keras import. No model, data, optimizer or metric changes.

Two classifier-head choices differ from the paper's statements. Transfer models: the paper fine-tunes each pretrained model 'using an added dense layer and one classification layer' (width not reported); this implementation connects pooled backbone features or the ViT class token directly to the 32-class softmax (scripts/models.py). CNN-3: Table 4 lists five convolutions followed by 'fully connected layer + softmax'; this implementation adds Dense(128) before the softmax, giving 519,628 parameters against 431,146 trainable parameters for CNN-3V4 in Table 4 (about 440,000 without Dense(128)). Human reviewer judgment (2026-11-04): the head differences are minor for CNN-3 and all transfer models except VGG16 and VGG19. For VGG, the missing added dense layer left the classifier with too few parameters; the reviewer attributes the observed single-class collapse to it and excludes the VGG accuracy targets. The attribution has not been tested with a corrected run.
